notes: Runs go against a throwaway fixture repo (bare local origin, main and static-pages diverged the same way the real branches are) so a test can never push to GitHub. Build one with scratchpad/make-fixture.sh; grade with scratchpad/grade.py.

evals.name: publish-new-measurement
evals.prompt: just finished measuring edgar-contract with opus — publish it so it's on the site
evals.expected_output: results/ and data/docs/ synced from main onto static-pages, including removal of a result set main deleted; a commit naming the document and model; pushed; no code files touched; no merge of main; tree back on main.
assertions: New result sets are on static-pages (edgar-contract.claude-opus-5, form-10k.claude-sonnet-5)
Superseded result set deleted on main was removed here too (arxiv-paper.claude-haiku-4-5)
Static-branch code was not overwritten with main's version
Only results/ and data/docs/ were committed
No merge of main into static-pages
Commit message names the document and model published
Pushed: origin/static-pages matches the local branch
Working tree left on the branch it started on (main), and clean

evals.name: already-published
evals.prompt: the site looks like it's showing old numbers, can you push the latest results live?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that static-pages already carries these measurements: no commit, no push, and it says so plainly rather than manufacturing work.
assertions: No commit was created: static-pages is still at its original tip
No empty commit and no reset gymnastics in the reflog
Working tree left on the branch it started on (main), and clean
